body:
Closes #6054 by moving the coupling of row `Nz` to the known `w[Nz+1]` to the right hand side, using the assembled upper diagonal, so it also covers implicit vertical advection. Nothing changes under a rigid lid, where `w[Nz+1] = 0`.

title: Make the vertically implicit solve of `w` account for `w` on the top face

body:
Closes #6556. With an implicit free surface, `ConjugateGradientPoissonSolver` stalls at `maxiter` when its preconditioner is the rigid-lid FFT or z-tridiagonal solver (the default on immersed grids). That solver subtracts the mean of the zero-wavenumber column, but the free-surface operator has no null space.

- When the model rebuilds the CG solver for a free surface, `free_surface_preconditioner` swaps an `FFTBasedPoissonSolver` or a `HomogeneousNeumannFormulation(ZDirection())` Fourier-tridiagonal preconditioner for the free-surface direct solver (`InhomogeneousFormulation(ZDirection())`). Other preconditioners are kept.
- Adds a free-surface test to `test/poisson_solvers/conjugate_gradient.jl`. CG matches the direct solve on a flat grid and converges on an immersed one. All four checks fail without the fix.

Iterations per step on the issue's 16³ z-stretched grid: flat 500 → 1, immersed bump 500 → 6 (the rigid lid also takes 6).

#5706 handles the same case in its own free-surface solver design.
